Filed from the P6-188 adversarial review (2026-08-09). Three real-but-not-blocking items: (1) teardown has no to_collection_id != collection_id guard, so it can write a from==to ledger row — the only source of the self-move rows the delete planner now defends against; add the guard. (2) delete_collection's FOR UPDATE covers only the subject collection row; a concurrent add_holding into the collection between snapshot and the deleted_at stamp is silently hidden (and a concurrently-hidden child can appear in the receipt's reparented list without having been re-parented) — alpha-tolerable single-user race; consider locking holdings or re-checking counts before commit. (3) the delete planner's apply() model ignores boards, so the destination-side Board::Main collapse in the executor is exercised only by the #[ignore]d delete_live dev test, never in CI — extend the planner model or add a board-aware no-DB test. Also note: the wire change (POST body now required) 422s a stale rolling APK posting the old empty body — self-heals on next APK install, alpha-acceptable.

Appended from the P6-190 round-2 review (2026-08-10): (4) undo_delete's desire re-insert (DO UPDATE SET quantity = quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity) can overflow int4 on a near-i32::MAX crafted receipt — rolls back, nothing stored, but surfaces as an Upstream 500 instead of a Validation 400; add an upper bound or catch the overflow into a typed error. (5) accepted-widening note: reparent_is_safe admits current-siblings (with reparent_to = None, every top-level non-Inbox collection) — verified acyclic and drag-repairable, deliberately NOT tightened because the delete destroys the was-actually-a-child fact; revisit only if the receipt ever records child ids explicitly. Specs: specs/collection-deletion.md.
